complexity.notes: word_tuple is recomputed for every word (once when seeding the dict, once when appending), so each string is scanned twice; a single loop with d.setdefault(sig, []).append(word) avoids that. The `tuple(int)` annotation is not a valid type expression, but under PEP 649 it is never evaluated, so it's harmless — still, `tuple[int, ...]` would be the idiomatic spelling. Since word lengths are constant in the scaling model, both the signature build and the dict work are O(1) per word, giving linear average time.
complexity.summary: Builds a 26-element letter-count tuple as each word's anagram signature, keys a dict on it, then appends every word to its signature's list in a second pass.
